blocks.h: Shia khums: how it is divided

head: Share
Goes to

Twelver Shia Muslims

questions.q: Describe the nature of khums in Shia Islam. (4 marks, our own question)
questions.a: One fifth of surplus annual income after expenses; paid yearly; divided into sahm al-Imam (to a marja') and sahm as-sadat (needy descendants of the Prophet ﷺ); based on 8:41.
questions.model: One mark per point: 1) a fifth (20%); 2) of surplus income after yearly living costs; 3) half to the Imam's share via a marja'; 4) half to needy sayyids, based on 8:41.

questions.q: In Sunni fiqh, khums applies to ...
questions.a: Spoils of war and buried treasure
options: Spoils of war and buried treasure

questions.q: Write a 6-mark answer in the portal response box (our own question): 'Explain the purpose of khums for Shia Muslims.' Then add one sentence on how Sunni Muslims understand 8:41. Start: 'One purpose of khums is ...'
questions.a: Supports religious scholarship and institutions through sahm al-Imam; supports needy descendants of the Prophet ﷺ through sahm as-sadat; purifies wealth; based on 8:41; Sunni sentence accurate
questions.model: Teacher writes point 1: 'One purpose of khums is to support religious learning. Shia Muslims give the sahm al-Imam to a senior scholar, who uses it for seminaries and centres.'

questions.q: why can sayyids not receive zakah in either tradition?
questions.a: Zakah is not permitted for the family of the Prophet ﷺ (Muslim); khums provides for them in Shia practice

questions.q: Back to our ponder: how should both views be described?
